summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 15, part 115) in which Emma and Ray dine at an Italian restaurant run by the exuberant Gino. Emma, uneasy, insists she is sheltered and unsophisticated, and deflects Ray's teasing about Amah. She explains that Amah's family has been part of the Whiston family from the beginning, and sketches the family's origins as a rescue from a plague-stricken Polynesian island and a founding investment by Grandfather Elliot George. The passage ends mid-sentence as the family history begins.
one_line: Emma and Ray dine at Gino's Italian restaurant, where Emma reveals her unease about the Whiston family and Amah's long history with them.
key_facts: Gino is described as dark and burly, bona fide Italian, and a whirlwind of jovial service at the restaurant.
Gino recommends linguini al sugo di pescatore and Sicilian mostacciolo.
Ray says the reception he received explains Amah's wariness, because Amah is afraid he will steal Emma away.
Ray lists reasons for possible rejection, including that he snores, his feet smell bad, and he sleeps with his socks on.
Emma says she has been very sheltered and that most of her life was spent on a frontier colony with fewer than a million people.
Emma says she is not sophisticated and has not traveled.
Emma says that in many ways Amah is more Whiston than any of the family.
Emma says Amah has held the family together for years, longer than Emma has been alive.
Emma does not meet Ray's gaze when she talks about the family, Frederick, or anything Whiston.
Amah's family has been with the Whiston family as long as there has been a Whiston family in the modern sense of financial juggernauts.
Amah's family was rescued by a great-great-grandfather from a plague-stricken Polynesian island.
Grandfather Elliot George sells everything he owns in Old Boston to purchase a majority share in a business.
Ray does not prompt Emma, sensing she has long waited to tell someone about the family.
